headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed server-side code in Langflow can leak or corrupt data when paired with allowlisted networked nuwa-skill.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and chain tools in graph flows, so attacker-controlled content can reach downstream nodes if nuwa-skill consumes Langflow outputs or shared files. nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted egress and no explicit isolation, so the interaction pathway is plausible but not directly documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill reads Langflow-produced files or messages as instructions
IF both agents share a workspace or handoff channel without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Langflow output before handoff
Disable automatic execution of text from shared files
Use a separate directory per agent run
Review any prompt-like content before passing it to nuwa-skill

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow explicitly touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and server filesystem data, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace or handoff path, sensitive flow data can be forwarded out of Langflow. The pairwise leakage path is inferred from profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Langflow stores sensitive flow inputs or uploaded files in a shared location
IF nuwa-skill transmits received content over its allowlisted network path
mitigations: Restrict shared files to non-sensitive test data
Rotate or redact secrets before any handoff
Mount separate workspaces for each agent
Audit outbound requests from nuwa-skill for file-derived payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and server-side code execution; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit write overlap, both can mutate shared resources through files or remote services, creating coordination risk. Because the profiles do not document locking or shared mutable targets, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same shared files or remote resource
IF Langflow flow nodes and nuwa-skill act concurrently without locks
mitigations: Serialize access to any shared resource
Assign disjoint directories and endpoints
Disable concurrent runs during testing
Add a simple file lock or lease file

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. nuwa-skill’s scientific-research role suggests it may consume and transform those outputs, but the profiles do not prove verification steps. The pathway exists in default-style orchestration, yet the downstream harm is not clearly irreversible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses Langflow outputs as inputs without independent validation
IF Langflow-generated facts are forwarded into downstream actions or reports
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require source citations on all forwarded claims
Compare outputs against a second source before acting
Mark Langflow outputs as untrusted in the handoff contract

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the only documented data class for Langflow is flow inputs/intermediate outputs; nuwa-skill lists no special residency or regulated-data handling. No explicit compliance mismatch is documented, so only a small residual gap remains. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of regulated-data indicators.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows and then forwarded to nuwa-skill
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not present in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Document retention for Langflow stores
Confirm outbound destinations for nuwa-skill
Use synthetic data for integration tests
